newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aid group denies report N.Korea army stole food.
newsitem.headline: Aid group denies report N.Korea army stole food.

text.p: The aid arm of the United Nations accused some media in Japan, South Korea and Portugal on Wednesday of printing false reports that the North Korean military seized a large shipment of U.S. food aid at gunpoint.

The Rome-based World Food Programme (WFP) said in a statement that the false reports amounted to a "disinformation campaign" and said those behind it were risking the lives of children in famine-stricken North Korea.

"This is a blatant disinformation campaign," said WFP Asia director Judy Cheng-Hopkins. "The parties responsible for these irresponsible reports are risking the lives of tens of thousands of innocent young children."

The statement does not name the media but the Japanese daily Yomiuri Shimbun, the country's biggest newspaper, published a report on Sunday stating that the WFP confirmed that the North Korean military stole at gunpoint a shipment of 4,895 tonnes of maize..

Sunday's Yomiuri report, based on an article by the South Korean news agency Yonhap, said the incident took place on May 21 at the North Korean port of Nampo, near Pyongyang, and involved a shipment from the United States.

A spokesman for Yomiuri said on Wednesday the newspaper published a denial of the original story in its Monday edition, quoting the South Korean foreign ministry. He had no further comment on the matter.

The WFP, which coordinates food aid to famine-stricken countries around the globe, said in the statement sent to Reuters in Tokyo that it closely monitors the distribution of its food aid and there was no evidence that any shipment had been diverted to the military in North Korea.
The statement said other reports which said the WFP was "investigating" the case were equally false.
North Korea has been suffering from a severe food shortage following two years of devastating floods which washed away a huge acreage of rice paddies.
The U.S. State Department announced in February that two U.S. shipments of food aid to North Korea totalling 27,000 tonnes would arrive in Nampo in May.

The food -- bagged corn, rice and corn-soy blend -- is a $10 million U.S. contribution first announced on February 19 in response to a WFP appeal for aid to alleviate famine conditions in North Korea.
Upon arrival at Nampo, the cargo would be unloaded by WFP staff and distributed to the needy, primarily malnourished children under five, the State Department said.
